title: Impact of oral vitamin K2 supplementation on blood and tissue biomarkers in patients with severe aortic valve stenosis
summary:
Aortic valve stenosis (AVS) is the most common valvular heart disease requiring treatment in industrialised countries. In its severe form, about 60% of those affected die within two years. Although the disease is common and associated with substantial impairment of health and an increased risk of death, there are currently no medications that can effectively stop its progression. There is evidence that vitamin K – particularly vitamin K2 – may have a beneficial effect on the aortic valve in the setting of a narrowing of the aortic valve (aortic valve stenosis). In this study we therefore aim to investigate how vitamin K2 affects certain processes in the blood and in the tissue of the aortic valve. To this end, in patients with aortic valve stenosis who have previously taken vitamin K2 or a preparation without an active ingredient for at least 6 weeks, we analyse the aortic valve that is removed during the heart valve replacement surgery. After removal, the valve tissue is examined in the laboratory under the microscope. In addition, we measure various biological markers that are associated with calcification of the valve.
We also examine the activity of certain genes in the valve cells. This allows us to better understand which processes take place within the cells and how vitamin K2 may influence them. The results of these investigations are intended to provide important insights into whether vitamin K2 can bring about changes in the valve tissue and whether it could help promote processes that counteract calcification and inflammation of the aortic valve. Depending on the results, we plan a larger follow-up study to investigate these relationships further.

interventions.name:
Experimental intervention: 
Intake of one capsule with 1mg vitamin K2 (Menaquinone-7) once daily for at least 6 weeks

Control intervention:
Intake of one capsule placebo once daily for at least 6 weeks

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
•	The patient has given written consent to participate in the clinical trial.
•	Confirmed diagnosis of severe aortic valve stenosis
•	Indication for surgical aortic valve replacement by decision of the local Heart Team
Exclusion criteria:
•	Patients  without legal capacity who are unable to understand the nature, scope, significance and consequences of this trial
•	Patients with a physical or psychiatric condition which at the investigator’s discretion may put the patient at risk, may confound the trial results, or may interfere with the patient’s participation in this trial
•	Participation in a clinical trial taking an investigational product, where the last IMP intake took place no more than 30 days ago
•	Known or persistent abuse of medication, drugs or alcohol
•	Current or planned pregnancy or nursing women
•	Females of childbearing potential, who are not using and are not willing to use medically reliable methods of contraception for the entire trial duration unless they are surgically sterilized / hysterectomized or there are any other criteria considered sufficiently reliable by the investigator in individual cases
•	Known history of hypersensitivity to the vitamin K2 supplement or to substances with a similar chemical structure
•	History of uncontrolled chronic disease or a concurrent clinically significant illness or medical condition, which in the investigator’s opinion, would contraindicate trial participation or compliance with protocol mandated procedures
•	Known prothrombotic coagulation disorders
•	Suspected or confirmed infectious endocarditis
•	Planned aortic valve replacement of a degenerated valve prothesis
•	Use of vitamin K antagonists
•	Regular intake of vitamin K supplements until trial participation
•	Hemodynamic Instability
